sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Reform UK Leaders Caught on Camera Making Graphic Threats
cards.content: Reform UK is facing a major crisis after its councillors and election candidates were caught making graphic threats of violence expressing racist and misogynistic views on camera. Three councillors have already left the party and leader Nigel Farage has postponed a big announcement to deal with the fallout. The party is trying to contain the damage as more revelations are expected to come out in the coming days including footage of senior politicians and officials at its UK headquarters.

cards.title: UK Gains Powers to Punish Settlement Supporters and Obstruct Aid
cards.content: The UK is giving itself new powers to freeze assets and punish entities that support Israeli settlements or obstruct humanitarian aid. This includes freezing assets and travel bans for people and companies that help these settlements or block aid. The new powers also allow the UK to punish people who incite or promote these actions even if they're not directly involved. This is part of a global human rights and humanitarian law sanctions regime that will start on Thursday but it needs approval from parliament within 28 days.

cards.title: US Military Plans Strikes on Iran Using "Mother of All Bombs"
cards.content: The US military has developed new strike plans that include using the "mother of all bombs" to target Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites. The plans are for President Donald Trump to give the order to resume combat operations before or after the midterm elections. The "mother of all bombs" is the largest non-nuclear bomb in the US arsenal and is designed to clear a huge area. If used it would likely only damage the surface level and could have devastating effects on the area. Some officials question whether the White House has a strategy that incorporates these plans in a way that could actually end the war.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Doctors Use Metagenomics to Quickly Diagnose Serious Infections
cards.content: Doctors are now using a technique called metagenomics to quickly diagnose serious infections. This test looks at all the DNA and RNA in a sample not just known pathogens. It helped identify Covid-19 and is now used in hospitals to diagnose things like sepsis and unexplained illnesses. The test can identify the exact organisms present allowing doctors to treat patients more effectively. It's already saved lives by helping doctors make life-or-death decisions.

cards.title: Scientists Reconstruct Ancient Middle Eastern Ecosystem 700,000 Years Ago
cards.content: Scientists have reconstructed the environment of early humans who lived in the Middle East nearly 700000 years ago. They studied the remains of giant elephants and found clues about the watery world they lived in which had plenty of water plants and animals. The area called Gesher Benot Ya'aqov was a stable ecosystem with woodlands grasslands and marshes where the elephants and early humans could survive.

cards.title: Seychelles Tortoise Population Reaches 183,000, Thanks to Conservation Efforts
cards.content: Giant tortoises on a Seychelles atoll are now estimated to be nearly 183000 which is more than the human population of the country. This is a significant recovery since the 19th century when exploitation reduced their numbers to fewer than 1000. The tortoises' population has remained relatively stable over the past five years and their abundance is attributed to decades of protection and conservation efforts.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case, Linked to Fatal First Case
cards.content: Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola a 39-year-old man who was already in quarantine when he fell ill. This case is linked to the first case a 40-year-old man who died on October 5. The new patient's early diagnosis has improved his chances of recovery and reduced the risk of him spreading the virus to others.

cards.title: Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case, 39-Year-Old Man in Quarantine
cards.content: Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola 10 days after a businessman died of the virus. The new patient is a 39-year-old man who is a close relative of the first case and was already in quarantine when he fell ill. He was in quarantine because he was a contact of the first case and detecting his illness early improved his chances of recovery.

cards.title: Boy Kibble Diet Gains Popularity for High-Protein Convenience
cards.content:
Here is a summary of the news article in one natural paragraph

Boy kibble is a way of eating that has become popular on social media where people strip meals back to basics to get high protein and convenience. It's a batch-cooked meal typically made with rice and ground meat with some people adding avocado for healthy fat. The diet has been popular among men especially those looking to increase their fitness as it provides a reliable way to meet protein goals. However experts warn that the diet can be imbalanced with too much protein and not enough vegetables and recommend adding some variety to the meals.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: North India Braces for Thunderstorms, Hailstorms and Heavy Rainfall
cards.content: North India is bracing for thunderstorms hailstorms lightning and heavy rainfall which may cause damage to crops infrastructure and disrupt daily life. The India Meteorological Department has issued a warning advising people to be cautious. Meanwhile southern India is preparing for the onset of the northeast monsoon which may bring heavy rainfall to some areas.

cards.title: Zimbabwe Plans $500 Million Reserve for Food Security Amid Drought Risk
cards.content: Zimbabwe's finance minister Mthuli Ncube announced on October 14 that the country plans to create a $500 million reserve of cash and grain to help with food security if a drought happens due to El Niño. This plan was approved by the Cabinet a month ago to prepare for the effects of a strong El Niño which could cause below-average rainfall long dry spells and higher temperatures during the next rainy season.

cards.title: Indonesia Reports 1.06 Million Wildfire Hotspots, 896,000 Hectares Burned
cards.content: As of October 14 Indonesia has detected over 1.06 million wildfire hotspots surpassing the 885000 recorded in 2019. So far nearly 896000 hectares of land have burned mostly due to dry conditions and slash-and-burn practices. The situation is made worse by the ongoing Super El Niño which could make the fires harder to control and increase the risk of new outbreaks. Smoke from the fires has already spread to neighboring Malaysia and Singapore affecting air quality and public health.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: La Bola Negra Nominated for Best Picture Academy Awards
cards.content: A film called La Bola Negra is a contender for the Academy Awards' best picture prize. The movie tells three stories of gay men across a century in Spain exploring themes of love repression and self-punishment. The film has received critical acclaim and is a commercial hit in Spain. It's known for its beautiful visuals complex storyline and courage in showing sexual desire. The directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi have been praised for their work and the film's cast including Álvaro Lafuente Calvo and Carlos González have also received recognition.

cards.title: Lena Dunham Revives Girls for Limited Run with Original Cast
cards.content: Lena Dunham the creator of the popular TV show Girls announced that the show will return for a limited run after a 10-year hiatus. The revival will feature five episodes and reunite the original cast including Allison Williams Jemima Kirke Zosia Mamet and Andrew Rannells. Dunham said she's been missing the characters and that they started talking to her again around her 40th birthday. The show will explore what's happened to the characters since they were in their 20s.

cards.title: Rob Brydon Voices New Animated "The Baddies" Adaptation
cards.content: Welsh actor Rob Brydon is voicing a new animated adaptation of the popular children's book "The Baddies" over the Christmas period. The story follows a troll a ghost and a witch as they try to steal a blue spotty hanky from a brave little girl. Brydon will be joined by Gavin and Stacey co-stars Sheridan Smith and Alison Steadman as well as Hammed Animashaun Robyn Cara and Francesca Mills. The half-hour special celebrates kindness and standing up to bullies and features beautiful animation.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: IMF Praises UK's Fiscal Strategy, Hails Debt Reduction Plans
cards.content: The International Monetary Fund is warning about the debts of the world's biggest economies. The UK is doing well compared to others with plans to reduce its borrowing costs and debt. The IMF likes the UK's approach and says it could lead to better growth prospects. This is good news for the UK's government but it might mean they have less money to spend or raise taxes.

cards.title: Netflix Cuts 1000 Jobs, Mostly HR and Tech Staff
cards.content: Netflix is cutting 1000 jobs about 6% of its workforce as it faces competition from other streaming services. The cuts will mainly affect teams that handle human resources legal product and technology issues. This is the biggest job cut at Netflix since 2022. The company's leaders said the move is necessary to focus on areas that will drive growth and innovation and that Netflix is still on track to meet its financial forecasts.

cards.title: US Inflation Surges to 3.7% as Petrol Prices Jump 34.2%
cards.content: US inflation rose more than expected to 3.7% in the year to September driven by higher petrol prices. This is the highest rate in a while with energy prices jumping 20.4% over the year. The increase was mostly due to a big surge in petrol prices which rose 34.2% over 12 months. Experts think the US Federal Reserve will be closely watching to see if energy costs start affecting other areas of the economy like food prices.
